title: Crown Root Initiation and Critical Irrigation Scheduling in Wheat
source: ICAR - Indian Agricultural Research Institute (IARI), New Delhi
content: Wheat requires 4 to 6 irrigations of 6-7 cm depth depending on soil type and winter rainfall. Six physiological critical stages for irrigation: 1. Crown Root Initiation (CRI) at 20-25 days after sowing (DAS) - MOST CRITICAL, 2. Tillering stage (40-45 DAS), 3. Jointing stage (60-65 DAS), 4. Flowering stage (80-85 DAS), 5. Milking stage (100-105 DAS), and 6. Dough stage (115-120 DAS). If only one irrigation is available, apply it strictly at CRI stage (yield penalty without CRI is up to 40%). If two irrigations available: apply at CRI and Flowering stages. If three irrigations available: CRI, Jointing, and Milking stages. Precautions: Avoid heavy irrigation during milking and grain filling on windy days to prevent crop lodging (falling over). Do not irrigate when field shows waterlogging symptoms as wheat roots are highly sensitive to poor aeration.
